sentences.text:
Order 
This is first bail application filed by the applicant under Section 439 of Criminal Procedure Code,
1973 for grant of regular bail relating to FIR/Crime No.383/2023 dated 30.9.2023 registered at Police Station - Bichhiya, District Mandla for the offence under Sections 363, 366, 366A, 376(2)(n)
of IPC and Section 5 L and 6 of the POCSO Act.
2. Learned counsel for the applicant contends that the prosecutrix and applicant have entered into wedlock on 25.6.2024.
A Marriage Certificate to that effect is brought on record vide Annexure A-2.

The Trial Court while rejecting the bail application of the applicant persuaded by the fact that when the offence was committed the prosecutrix was minor as she was aged about 17 years, three months and 11 days.
It is contended by the counsel that the applicant himself is aged about 23 years and the prosecutrix at the time of commission of offence was aged about 17 years and three months.

Therefore, the applicant who has no criminal past and is in custody since NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2024:MPHC-JBP:40442 2 MCRC-34703-2024 27.7.2024 deserves to be enlarged on bail.
3. Learned counsel for the State has opposed the prayer for grant of bail and submitted that considering the nature of allegation, no case for grant of bail is made out.

4. Considering the totality of the circumstances and also the fact that the applicant and prosecutrix Bhupendra Kumar Paraste vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 14 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/178913211/
1 have entered into wedlock on 25.6.2024, this Court deem it fit to enlarge the applicant on bail.

entities.text: Bhupendra Kumar Paraste vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 5. It is directed that the applicant shall be released on bail on his furnishing personal bond in a sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) with solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court concerned their appearance before the said Court on all such dates as may be fixed in this regard during the pendency of trial.

6. It is further directed that the applicants shall comply with the provisions of Section 437 (3) of the Cr.P.C.
7.
Accordingly, this M.Cr.C. stands allowed and disposed of.
(MANINDER S. BHATTI) JUDGE VKT Bhupendra Kumar Paraste vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 14 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/178913211/
